page.layout: One title page. Above: the title in capitals, five centred lines, the last with "AUTHORE" and the author's name. Middle: an italic statement of content, then a woodcut with "IESVS" and a Latin motto below it. Foot: place and printer's imprint, centred. No margins, running head or page number.

Ecce agnus ille Dei,qui tollit peccatum mundi.

page.notes: The woodcut (between the statement and "IESUS") shows a tree with spreading branches, a seated or kneeling figure with a staff, a child-like figure, a town with a tower in the background, and a lamb or animal at the lower right. It is an illustration, not text. The "&" before "locorum" is a ligature-like sign that I could not read with certainty. The spacing "Dei,qui" in the motto appears to lack a space in print. Upper-case V has been normalised to U for vowels (AUTHORE, GUALTHERO, TIGURINO, IESUS, etc.), as the rules require.
